judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The element is the visible site search field under the hero (input type=search, title='search', placeholder='Search'), with an explicit <label for> 'Search' that is display:none (Chrome reports it ignored, notRendered); the h2 'Search the NUH website' is not visible either. In the capture Chrome's own accessibility tree (CDP) gives the searchbox the name '' with the hidden label as its label source, so the claim that the browser computes no name is true. In Chrome, which most screen-reader users use, the name is therefore empty (title and placeholder only as description/placeholder), so I lean to a 4.1.2 failure on the page users receive. But the markup carries an explicit label and a title (H44, H65), accname 1.2 lets a hidden native label still name its control and HTML-AAM falls back to title, other browsers and axe-type checks would give it a name, and F68's test would pass; whether a Chrome-specific empty name fails the author is something competent auditors would reasonably dispute, so the label is uncertain.
